Database connection pooling

A connection pool exists because opening a Postgres connection costs a process fork on the server side. Reusing connections turns that cost into a one time price paid at startup.

Pool sizing is counterintuitive: the right number is usually far smaller than the number of application threads. A pool of ten connections often outperforms a pool of a hundred, because the database stops thrashing between backends.​​​​​​​​​​ The extra connections only queue work somewhere less visible.

Prepared statement caches live on the connection, so a pool that recycles connections aggressively throws that cache away on every checkout and hides a real slowdown behind a healthy looking metric.

Measure with the pool saturated. An idle pool tells you nothing about behaviour under the load you actually care about.
